descriptor.scene: There is no human being anywhere in this frame. EVERY SINGLE FIGURE in this picture is a factory manager of the same one design: a small blocky luminous plum-glowing mascot in a cream newsboy cap, identical to the last, repeated hundreds of times. No other kind of figure, no other colour of glow, no other hat. The camera is well back and a little high and THE HALL is the subject: one enormous warm hall at night, honey-wood floor, cream walls, a high vaulted ceiling of pale timber, warm amber lamps hung in long rows. Hundreds of managers stand and sit across the floor in easy clusters of three and four, at full length and small, turned toward one another, comparing notes: some with a mitten arm raised mid-explanation, some listening, a few standing up on low wooden platforms so their own cluster can see them. Small plain open log books lie about among them. Their hundreds of plum glows together light the hall from below like a field of lanterns while the amber lamps warm it from above. The mood is awe and ease: the clusters are spaced with clear warm floor between them and the hall is far bigger than the gathering, never a crowd crushed together, never a rally, no stage and nobody addressing the rest. Composition: the hall opens away from the camera toward a far wall; the NEAREST cluster in the lower centre is drawn a little larger than the rest so the one repeated design reads clearly, cap and plum body and mitten stubs all legible; the upper right stays calm lit ceiling and lamplight.
descriptor._caption: Then night comes, and the managers dream. Every manager from every machine of TastefulStories gathers in one warm hall, hundreds of plum glows and cream caps, and they compare notes. Who found a shorter way. Whose gate caught something new. It is a performance review, and nobody dreads it, because nobody is on trial. The factory is.
negatives: any figure that is not a plum-glowing mascot in a cream newsboy cap
differing hats, colours or body designs among the managers
an admiral hat, a laurel sprig, a gold ribbon bookmark or eyeglasses on any figure
a crowd crushed shoulder to shoulder
a rally, a stage, a podium or one figure addressing the rest
a human being of any kind

The output has exactly ONE camera, ONE moment, and NO internal borders, frames, gutters, or dividing lines of any kind. SPEAKER AND AUDIENCE GEOMETRY. Someone addressing a group FACES that group, and the group FACES THEM BACK. The two are on OPPOSITE sides of one another, never on the same side. So there are exactly TWO legal cameras and you must pick one of them. EITHER the camera is BEHIND OR AMONG THE AUDIENCE, in which case the audience fills the near foreground SEEN FROM BEHIND (backs of heads and shoulders) and the speaker stands beyond them FACING THE CAMERA. OR the camera is AT THE SPEAKER, in which case we see the speaker from behind or in three-quarter rear view and the audience beyond them is TURNED TOWARD THE CAMERA with their FACES VISIBLE. THE AUDIENCE IS NEVER ARRAYED BEHIND THE SPEAKER, never scattered around them, and never seated facing the same direction the speaker faces. A speaker with listeners behind their shoulders has their back turned on the people they are talking to, which is not what the scene means. A NAMED CHARACTER SITTING IN A CROWD IS STILL PART OF THAT CROWD. When someone the story cares about is among an audience, congregation, class or crowd, they FACE THE SAME WAY EVERYONE ELSE FACES and hold the same posture as the people around them. They are NOT turned out toward the camera while the rest of the room faces the speaker, NOT swivelled in their seat, NOT leaning into the aisle, NOT lit differently, NOT haloed, and NOT given more space around them than their neighbours. A figure facing a different direction from everyone around them reads as detached from the room, or as though they are looking at something nobody else can see. IF THE SCENE NEEDS THEIR FACE, MOVE THE CAMERA, NOT THE PERSON: shoot the crowd from in front or from the side so their face is naturally visible while they still face what everyone else faces. Make them findable by PLACEMENT and by what they wear, never by breaking the room's shared orientation.
